This guide uses the bundled Cornwall GP data, described in [The Cornwall GP
example data](cornwall-data.html).

This guide runs the experimental allocation workflow from start to finish:
prepare inputs, declare a model, fit it to observed registrations, inspect the
saved fit, predict at new locations, compare a change in one practice's supply,
and export the results and read them back in a fresh R session. Bootstrap
intervals have their own guide, [Bootstrap intervals for a fitted allocation
model](facility-bootstrap.html), on generated data.

The model is a corrected static conditional logit (CLM) with an explicit
outside option. Each practice attracts residents in proportion to its supply,
discounted by travel time; the outside option competes with all practices. For
choosing between this model and an FCA index, see [Choosing an FCA index or an
allocation model](model-choice.html). [Preparing your own
data](data-prep.html) explains counts, units, IDs and missing travel, and
[saved-result inspection](function-naming.html) describes the
standard R methods used below. The interface is experimental.

```{r packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(spax)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The data

The model uses four of the bundled objects: small areas with their registered
residents (`cornwall_lsoa`), practices with their GP full-time equivalents
(FTE, `cornwall_gp`), registrations by small area and practice
(`cornwall_flows`) and travel minutes between them (`cornwall_travel`). As in
the other guides, it covers mainland Cornwall only, because the Isles of
Scilly have no road link to the mainland.

```{r inputs}
# Mainland small areas and practices, as plain tables
areas <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
gp <- cornwall_gp |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

# Travel minutes: small areas in rows, practices in columns
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]

# Demand: residents registered with any practice in England.
demand <- setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa)
# Supply: GP FTE excluding GPs in training.
supply <- setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)

# Observed flows: registered residents by small area (rows) and practice.
observed <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(travel),
  ncol = ncol(travel),
  dimnames = dimnames(travel)
)
keep <- cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% rownames(travel) &
  cornwall_flows$practice %in% colnames(travel)
observed[cbind(cornwall_flows$lsoa[keep], cornwall_flows$practice[keep])] <-
  cornwall_flows$patients[keep]

dim(travel)
c(registered = sum(demand), at_mainland_practices = sum(observed))
```

Registrations are a stock: who is registered where in July 2026, not a count
of visits. Because demand counts every registered resident, the outside option
stands for registration with a practice outside mainland Cornwall (in Devon,
for example, or on the Isles of Scilly). It is not unmet need: almost everyone
is registered with some practice.

## Prepare, declare and fit

`prepare_allocation()` aligns demand, supply and travel by their names and
checks them once. Unit and period labels are declarations attached to the
results; spax does not convert units. `clm_allocation()` then declares the
model: a Gaussian travel kernel with scale σ (minutes) and a fitted outside
weight v0.

```{r prepare}
# Labels kept with the inputs and every result derived from them
cornwall_units <- list(
  demand_units = "registered residents",
  demand_period = "July 2026",
  supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training",
  supply_period = "June 2026",
  travel_units = "minutes"
)

inputs <- prepare_allocation(
  demand = demand,
  supply = supply,
  distance = travel,
  metadata = cornwall_units
)

model <- clm_allocation(
  inputs = inputs,
  family = "gaussian",
  fit_v0 = TRUE  # estimate the outside weight
)
```

`fit_allocation()` runs one fit from each supplied start and keeps the best
converged one. Here the target is the small area × practice flow matrix and
the loss is Poisson, chosen explicitly: asking for counts does not choose a
likelihood. Registrations are not independent event counts, so treat the
Poisson loss as a fitting criterion rather than a full observation model.
Joint Poisson fitting does not force the modelled total to match the observed
total.

```{r fit}
# Three starting points, from a short to a long travel scale
starts <- rbind(
  near = c(sigma = 3, v0 = 0.05),
  middle = c(sigma = 6, v0 = 0.01),
  far = c(sigma = 12, v0 = 0.002)
)

fit <- fit_allocation(
  model = model,
  observed = observed,
  starts = starts,
  lower = c(sigma = 0.5, v0 = 1e-6),
  upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 10),
  output = "flow",  # fit the small area x practice matrix
  loss = "poisson",
  gradient = TRUE,
  control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8)
)

# Every start, then the selected parameters as a table
summary(fit)
as.data.frame(fit)
```

The summary keeps every start, its convergence, boundaries and messages. All
three starts converge away from the bounds and stop very close to each other,
but the disagreement flag uses deliberately strict default tolerances, so read
the gaps in the per-start table rather than the flag alone. Agreement among the
supplied starts is a numerical check; it does not prove a global optimum or
that the parameters are identified. A σ of about 4.4 minutes means
registration is very local: a practice 9 minutes away keeps only about 12% of
the pull it would have next door.

## Fitted against observed

`fitted()` returns the saved fitted flows; nothing is recomputed. Summing over
small areas gives each practice's modelled registered list.

```{r practice-fit, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.5}
# Observed and modelled list size of each practice
practices <- data.frame(
  practice = colnames(observed),
  observed = colSums(observed),
  fitted = colSums(fitted(fit))
)
cor(practices$observed, practices$fitted)

ggplot(practices, aes(observed / 1000, fitted / 1000)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Observed registered residents (thousands)",
    y = "Modelled registered residents (thousands)",
    title = "Practice lists from mainland residents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The model gives each practice an attraction proportional to its GP FTE and
uses only supply and travel. Practices with more registered patients per GP FTE
than their neighbours therefore have larger observed than modelled lists and
sit below the dashed line.

## What the observations identify

A good fit does not show that the travel kernel is right. `check_allocation()`
never changes the fit; it compares the fitted model, on the same loss, with the
same model without distance decay (each small area chooses among the practices it
can reach in proportion to GP FTE), and reports the one-way trips each
implies.

```{r check}
# The fit against an allocation without distance decay
check_allocation(model, fit)
```

Here the target is the small area × practice matrix, which records where each
practice's patients live, so dropping distance decay worsens the fit by a wide
margin, and the fitted model's trips are short (a median of a few minutes).
When only practice totals are observed, the check also fits an allocation that
shares the totals by capacity alone. If that, or the no-decay allocation, fits
at least as well as the model, the totals do not identify distance decay: the
fitted value then depends on which travel times were treated as reachable, not
on the counts.

The outside share is the other observable output. Each small area's modelled
outside share can be compared with the share of its residents registered
outside mainland Cornwall.

```{r outside-map, fig.height = 4.5}
# Solve the model once at the fitted parameters
evaluated <- evaluate_allocation(model = model, theta = coef(fit))

# Outside shares and flows for the fitted small areas
baseline <- predict_allocation(
  source = evaluated,
  distance = travel,
  demand = demand,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "flow")
)
table(baseline$validity$status)

# Observed and modelled outside shares in one long table
outside <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    lsoa = names(demand),
    share = 1 - rowSums(observed) / demand,
    source = "Observed"
  ),
  data.frame(
    lsoa = names(demand),
    share = baseline$outputs$outside_share,
    source = "Modelled"
  )
) |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, c("Observed", "Modelled")))

# Join to the small-area polygons for mapping
outside_map <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  select(lsoa) |>
  inner_join(outside, by = "lsoa")

ggplot(outside_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = 100 * share), colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako",
    direction = -1,
    trans = "sqrt",
    name = "Registered\noutside (%)"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Share of residents registered outside mainland Cornwall") +
  theme_void()
```

`evaluate_allocation()` solves the model once at fixed parameters; it estimates
nothing. `predict_allocation()` then returns the requested outputs for any set
of origins, with separate validity flags. Here `flow` is requested demand times
choice probability, in registered residents. Requested demand only scales the
predicted flows; it never changes the saved practice loads.

Observed registration outside mainland Cornwall is concentrated in a few areas
along the Devon border. A single constant outside weight cannot reproduce that
pattern: the model spreads a small outside share everywhere and puts its largest
values where practices are far away, so treat the modelled outside share as
approximate.

## Predict at new locations

Prediction does not need the fitted small areas. Each cell of the bundled
1 km population grid has its own travel times to every practice, so the saved
model can predict at every populated cell. A `spatial` mapping from requested
origins to raster cells turns one output into a map.

```{r grid-predict}
# Population grid, and the travel grid as a cell x practice matrix
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
grid_travel <- values(read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif"))

# Keep populated cells and the fitted practices, in the fitted order
populated <- which(is.finite(values(pop)[, 1]) & values(pop)[, 1] > 0)
grid_travel <- grid_travel[populated, colnames(travel)]
rownames(grid_travel) <- paste0("cell", populated)

# Predict at each cell; no demand is needed for probabilities
grid <- predict_allocation(
  source = evaluated,
  distance = grid_travel,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "allocation")
)
table(grid$validity$status)
```

Cells on the Isles of Scilly have no travel time to mainland practices, so
their prediction is marked unknown rather than imputed. Inspect these flags
before reading a map.

```{r grid-map, fig.height = 4}
# Which raster cell each requested origin belongs to
grid_spatial <- list(
  template = pop,
  cell_index = setNames(populated, rownames(grid_travel))
)

grid_outside <- predict_allocation(
  source = evaluated,
  distance = grid_travel,
  outputs = "outside_share",
  spatial = grid_spatial,
  type = "raster"  # return a map instead of a table
)
plot(
  grid_outside,
  axes = FALSE,
  col = hcl.colors(50, "Mako", rev = TRUE),
  main = "Modelled outside share (proportion), 1 km grid"
)

# Cells with an outside share above 0.5, and their share of the population
grid_pop <- values(pop)[populated, 1]
far_out <- grid$outputs$outside_share > 0.5
c(
  cells = sum(far_out, na.rm = TRUE),
  population_percent = round(
    100 * sum(grid_pop[which(far_out)]) / sum(grid_pop),
    2
  )
)
```

Some grid cells far from every practice get a high outside share because the
fitted travel scale is short and the outside weight is constant. The
`r sum(far_out, na.rm = TRUE)` cells above 0.5 hold
`r round(100 * sum(grid_pop[which(far_out)]) / sum(grid_pop), 2)`% of the
grid's population, but their values are an
extrapolation of the model, not a measure of unmet need. The grid population
(WorldPop 2020) and the registrations (NHS England 2026) are different sources
and dates, so the grid is used here only for locations.

## Change one practice's supply

A scenario changes the system and evaluates it again at the same parameters.
Here Marazion Surgery is closed by setting its GP FTE to zero; known zero
supply is kept, so the practice stays in the network with no attraction. This
is a model-based, fixed-parameter scenario, not an estimate of what a real
closure would cause: changing supply moves attraction, allocation and every
practice's modelled load together.

```{r scenario}
closed <- "L82047"
gp |>
  filter(practice == closed) |>
  pull(name)

# Same inputs, with zero GP FTE at the closed practice
scenario_supply <- supply
scenario_supply[closed] <- 0
scenario_model <- clm_allocation(
  inputs = prepare_allocation(
    demand = demand,
    supply = scenario_supply,
    distance = travel,
    metadata = cornwall_units
  ),
  family = "gaussian",
  fit_v0 = TRUE
)

# Evaluate at the fitted parameters; nothing is refitted
scenario <- evaluate_allocation(model = scenario_model, theta = coef(fit))
changed <- predict_allocation(
  source = scenario,
  distance = travel,
  demand = demand,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "flow")
)

# Modelled list sizes before and after
baseline_lists <- colSums(baseline$outputs$flow)
scenario_lists <- colSums(changed$outputs$flow)
practices <- practices |>
  mutate(
    baseline = baseline_lists,
    scenario = scenario_lists,
    change = scenario - baseline,
    name = gp$name[match(practice, gp$practice)]
  )

# The seven largest changes
practices |>
  arrange(desc(abs(change))) |>
  select(name, baseline, scenario, change) |>
  head(7)

# Change in the number of residents modelled outside mainland practices
c(
  outside_change = sum(demand * changed$outputs$outside_share) -
    sum(demand * baseline$outputs$outside_share)
)
```

The modelled list of the closed practice moves to nearby practices in
Penzance and St Ives Bay, with a small part going to the outside option. Where
a closed practice has no near neighbour, a larger part goes to the outside
option; that follows from the constant outside weight, not from evidence about
where patients would go.

```{r scenario-map, fig.height = 5}
# Each area's modelled share of residents at the closed practice
moved <- data.frame(
  lsoa = names(demand),
  share = baseline$outputs$flow[, closed] / demand
)
moved_map <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  select(lsoa) |>
  inner_join(moved, by = "lsoa")

# Practices that gain more than 10 modelled registrations, with locations
gained <- cornwall_gp |>
  select(practice) |>
  inner_join(
    practices |>
      filter(change > 10) |>
      select(practice, change),
    by = "practice"
  )

# Map window over west Cornwall, in British National Grid metres
west <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = 130000, ymin = 18000, xmax = 185000, ymax = 48000),
  crs = st_crs(cornwall_lsoa)
)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = moved_map,
    aes(fill = 100 * share),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.05
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = gained, aes(size = change), shape = 21, fill = "orange") +
  geom_sf(
    data = filter(cornwall_gp, practice == closed),
    shape = 4,
    size = 3,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako",
    direction = -1,
    name = "Residents at the\nclosed practice (%)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(name = "Modelled\nregistrations\ngained") +
  coord_sf(xlim = west[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = west[c("ymin", "ymax")]) +
  labs(
    title = "Closing Marazion Surgery (x): who moves and where to",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Modelled baseline share of residents at the practice;",
      "points are receiving practices"
    )
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## Save and reload

The evaluated scenario carries a small prediction snapshot. Saving it does not
keep the model or the travel matrix, and the restored object predicts the same
values.

```{r save-and-reload}
# Save the evaluated scenario and read it back
saved <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(scenario, saved)
restored <- readRDS(saved)

# The restored object predicts exactly what the original did
stopifnot(identical(
  predict_allocation(
    source = restored,
    distance = travel,
    demand = demand,
    outputs = c("outside_share", "flow")
  ),
  changed
))
unlink(saved)
```

## Export and reload in a fresh session

CSV files make saved tables available to other software but drop R classes and
attributes. Keep an RDS bundle alongside them to preserve the fit, declarations,
units and the complete results.

```{r export-saved-results}
export_dir <- tempfile("allocation-results-")
dir.create(export_dir)

# One CSV file per table
export_tables <- list(
  parameters = as.data.frame(fit),
  practices = practices
)
for (name in names(export_tables)) {
  write.csv(
    export_tables[[name]],
    file.path(export_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}

# One RDS bundle with the full R objects
bundle_path <- file.path(export_dir, "allocation-results.rds")
saveRDS(
  list(
    fit = fit,
    scenario = scenario,
    closed = closed,
    tables = export_tables
  ),
  bundle_path
)
list.files(export_dir)
```

Finally, a new R process with the installed package reads the bundle. It checks
the saved tables, predicts the scenario again from the bundled Cornwall travel
times, and prints and plots the saved fit without refitting.

```{r fresh-installed-reload}
# Write a short script for a new R process
child_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
literal <- function(x) paste(capture.output(dput(x)), collapse = "\n")
writeLines(c(
  # Use the same installed spax and read the bundle
  paste0(".libPaths(c(", literal(dirname(find.package("spax"))), ", .libPaths()))"),
  "library(spax)",
  paste0("saved <- readRDS(", literal(bundle_path), ")"),
  # The saved tables match the saved objects
  "stopifnot(identical(as.data.frame(saved$fit), saved$tables$parameters))",
  # Predict the closure scenario again from the bundled travel times
  "areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)",
  "gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)",
  "travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa[!areas$scilly], gp$practice[!gp$scilly]]",
  "demand <- setNames(areas$registered[!areas$scilly], areas$lsoa[!areas$scilly])",
  "flow <- predict_allocation(saved$scenario, travel, demand = demand, outputs = 'flow')$outputs$flow",
  "stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(colSums(flow)), unname(saved$tables$practices$scenario))))",
  "stopifnot(colSums(flow)[[saved$closed]] == 0)",
  # Summaries and plots work without refitting
  "stopifnot(inherits(summary(saved$fit), 'summary.ae_multistart_fit'))",
  "print(summary(saved$fit))",
  "plot_path <- tempfile(fileext = '.pdf')",
  "grDevices::pdf(plot_path)",
  "plot(saved$fit, type = 'fit')",
  "grDevices::dev.off()",
  "stopifnot(file.info(plot_path)$size > 0)",
  "unlink(plot_path)",
  "cat('Fresh installed saved-result inspection passed\\n')"
), child_path)

# Run it with a clean Rscript and stop if it fails
rscript <- file.path(
  R.home("bin"),
  if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") "Rscript.exe" else "Rscript"
)
status <- system2(rscript, c("--vanilla", shQuote(child_path)))
stopifnot(status == 0L)
unlink(child_path)
```
